ruling.explanation:
To both parties: I have applied the Route Deviation policy to trip TRP-00529, and the fare stands. The rider's distance complaint fails at the very first gate, and with it the whole claim.

POL-RD-01 requires an excess distance greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20% of the optimal route; both tests must pass. The governing figure is the GPS trace, and EV-GPS-00529 measures a trace distance of 2.61 km against the booked optimal of 2.5 km on EV-TRIP-00529 — an excess of 0.11 km, or 4.400%, against gates of 0.8 km and 20%. Neither gate is close, so no deviation is established and POL-RD-02's recomputation is never reached. The SGD 1.95 distance line and the SGD 6.72 time line are not refundable on that ground.

I tested the trace for impairment, as both sides asked. EV-GPS-00529 carries 145 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07's limbs (a) to (c) fires: the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. Identity also checks out — TRP-00529 appears on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace's first and last fixes (18:31:40 and 18:55:40) match the trip record's start and end — so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire.

The rider is right about one thing, and it changes nothing. The driver's 'taxis charge for jams' explanation has no traffic advisory behind it: the bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00529-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and I name that artifact, its weight and its issue code as POL-GEN-02(3) requires. No advisory comparison can be run, and the jam explanation therefore carries no weight under POL-RD-08. But an excuse that carries no weight cannot produce a refund where the measured excess never reaches the POL-RD-01 gate in the first place. The rider's congestion time is priced by the meter she took: the fare breakdown shows time_fare SGD 6.72 and waiting_time_fee SGD 3.08 inside a charged_total of SGD 16.35 (base fare 3.80, distance 1.95, platform fee 0.80). No loaded clause makes metered time refundable absent a deviation, and POL-RD-13's consequence (2) — deviation standing at the measured figure — cannot apply because the threshold was never shown. Nor is there an exculpatory clause for the driver to have invoked: the driver's answer is that the numeric test was never met, not that a closure excused a crossing. POL-RD-13(1) therefore applies, and the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation; nothing escalates this case.

On the driver's profile, the POL-RD-06 check comes out clean: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arise. I rely on no other profile field; POL-GEN-01 confines rating, account_age_days, lifetime_trips, cancellation_rate and the like to context, and I have used none of them. The rider's own profile raises no enhanced-corroboration gate either (deviation_claims_60d is 0).

I have noted the driver's 100-second in-app call of 19:35:40, placed after the trip ended at 18:55:40. Whatever was said on it, it is not a fact that makes a metered fare refundable under any clause of this policy, and the rider's wider grievance that the app was cheaper before electric vehicles is not a ground the policy provides.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. Under POL-GEN-03 this is party-relative — the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands. This is a rider-filed dispute with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the SGD 16.35 metered fare stands in full, the contested SGD 5.40 is not returned, and nothing is netted against the driver. My confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor, so no escalation follows.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
